newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian dlr consolidates ahead of U.S jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian dlr consolidates ahead of U.S jobs.

text.p: The Australian dollar had an uneventful day in local trading ahead of key U.S. payrolls data later on Friday, consolidating the gains of an overnight rally that saw it break through US$0.7930 resistance.

The AUD hit its highest levels in two months early in local trade on the back of the offshore buying, but lacked the impetus to break the US$0.7950/60 resistance area that would lead to the restarting of the uptrend from earlier in 1996, traders said.
By 4.30 p.m. (0630 GMT), the AUD was trading at US$0.7936/41, down on an opening US$0.7948/53 but up on Thursday's finish of US$0.7902/07.

The AUD received a boost overnight when it was bought against the USD and yen by offshore traders who reacted more favourably than local traders to comments from Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Bernie Fraser on Thursday that there appeared to be no need for an early change in monetary policy.
This took the unit through US$0.7930 setting off stop loss orders.
Early this morning, the AUD traded to a high of US$0.7960/65 but traders said it was unlikely the unit would break that resistance level ahead of the payrolls data.
U.S. payrolls are expected to show a rise of 244,000 in August, with a number above that seen fuelling the growing expectations that U.S. rates will be lifted in coming months.
With the USD also steady in Asian trading ahead of the release of payrolls data, the AUD also held up on the crosses, against which they had also strengthened in overnight trade.
The AUD was at 86.70/80 yen and 1.1789/1800 marks late on Friday, from opening rates of 86.81/91 and 1.1815/27 and well up on the 85.99/86.09 and 1.1693/1708 levels late on Thursday.
In trade weighted terms, the AUD was steady at 58.3 through the day after closing Thursday at 57.9
Next week, local labour force data will be released and it again is expected to show only moderate employment growth that will not make any inroads into the unemployment rate.

The stalling in unemployment was one of the key factors behind the RBA's decision to cut rates on July 31, and in his speech on Thursday Fraser said that apart from unemployment, forecasts for 1996/97 suggested a fairly comfortable year.

While it appeared there was little need for early policy action, Fraser said the policy makers would be alert for early signs of divergence from the official forecasts, with unemployment one of the three areas he specifically mentioned.

For this reason, a number on Thursday around the median forecast of a 12,000 rise in August employment and leaving the unemployment rate unchanged at 8.5 percent, will continue to fuel speculation that local rates will be cut in the December quarter, economists said.
Thursday will also see Fraser, and his successor Ian Macfarlane, before a parliamentary committee, with the markets waiting for any update in the rates outlook.
Talk of a cut would undermine support for the AUD, as it would narrow the attractive interest differentials the AUD now enjoys, traders said. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 373 1800
